title: Different Types of Texts
keyIdea: Stories, poems and fact books are different types of text. A story (fiction) has characters, and something happens to them. A poem has short lines and often rhymes. A fact book (non-fiction) gives true information about the real world. The cover can trick you, so look at the words inside for clues. The author writes the words and the illustrator draws the pictures; their names are on the front cover, and one person can do both jobs.

kid: There are different types of text. A story tells about characters, and something happens to them. A poem has short lines. It often rhymes, like cat and hat. A fact book tells true things about the real world.
You cannot always tell from the cover. A book with a lion on it could be a story about a lion who sings. Or it could be a fact book about real lions. Look at the words inside for clues.
Clues for a story: Once upon a time, and The end. Clues for a poem: short lines and words that rhyme. Clues for a fact book: true facts, labels on photos, and a page that lists what is inside.
Two people can make a book. The author writes the words. The illustrator draws the pictures. Look for their names on the front cover. Sometimes one person does both jobs.
adult: This topic matches the US Common Core reading standards for Kindergarten and Grade 1. RL.K.5 asks children to recognise common types of texts, such as storybooks and poems. RL.K.6 and RI.K.6 ask them to name the author and illustrator and say what each one does. RL.1.5 asks them to explain the main differences between books that tell stories and books that give information. In England, Year 1 pupils meet key stories, rhymes, poems and non-fiction, and learn to talk about them.

Useful terms: fiction, non-fiction, story, poem, rhyme, title, front cover, author, illustrator, contents page, label and caption. A story has characters, a setting and events, often with a problem and an ending. A poem is set out in short lines and plays with sound, through rhyme, rhythm and repeated words. A fact book is organised to inform, with headings, labelled pictures and a contents page.

Common mistakes: judging the type from the cover picture; thinking any book with pictures is a story; thinking the author draws the pictures; thinking every poem must rhyme, when many do not; and saying fiction means lies. Fiction is made up on purpose to entertain, which is different from telling a lie. Be careful with picture books too, where one person may be both author and illustrator.

In the lab your child sorts six books onto Story, Poem and Facts shelves, where a lizard on a cover tempts a wrong guess. They tap the clue on three pages, drag a pencil and a paintbrush tag to the author and the illustrator on two covers, tap the rhyming lines in a short poem, and then write and draw their own little book of two different types.

familyTip: At the library, pick three books together: a story, a book of poems and a fact book. Before you open each one, guess its type from the cover, then check the words inside and find the author and the illustrator.

visual.caption: Story, poem or facts? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: Once upon a time, a hen found some wheat.
The little pig ran away, and the wolf ran after him.
Jack and Jill went up the hill to fetch a pail of water.
Wiggle, wiggle, little worm, twist and turn and squirm.
Owls hunt at night and sleep in the day.
The heart pumps blood all round the body.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sort six books onto shelves, tap the clue on each page, tag the author and the illustrator, find rhymes, then make your own book.

practice.prompt: Which of these is from a poem?
choices: Twinkle, twinkle, little star, how I wonder what you are
Owls hunt at night and sleep in the day
Once upon a time, an owl lost her way home
practice.hint: Look for short lines and words that rhyme at the end.
practice.explain: Star and are rhyme, and it is said in a sing-song way. The owl facts are from a fact book, and once upon a time starts a story.

practice.prompt: A poem has {=2*n} lines. Each two lines rhyme as a pair. How many rhyming pairs are there?
practice.hint: Put the lines into twos: lines 1 and 2, lines 3 and 4, and so on.
practice.explain: {=2*n} lines in twos make {n} rhyming pairs.

practice.prompt: Who draws the pictures in a book?
practice.hint: One person writes the words and one person draws the pictures. Which name goes with pictures?
practice.explain: The illustrator draws the pictures. The author writes the words. Sometimes one person does both.

practice.prompt: A shelf has {a} books. {b} of them are stories and the rest are fact books. How many fact books are there?
practice.hint: Take the stories away from all the books on the shelf.

pool.prompt: A book says: Frogs lay eggs in water. Tadpoles hatch from the eggs. What type of text is it?
pool.hint: Are these true things about real animals, or is something made up happening to a character?
pool.explain: It tells true facts about real frogs, so it is a fact book. It has no characters and no rhyme.

pool.prompt: Sam wrote {a} poems. He drew the pictures for {b} of them, and Ann drew the rest. How many poems did Ann illustrate?
pool.hint: Ann drew the pictures for the poems Sam did not draw. Take {b} away from {a}.
pool.explain: {a} − {b} = {=a-b}. Ann is the illustrator of {=a-b} poems, and Sam is the author of all {a}.

pool.prompt: A book starts with Once upon a time. What type of text is it most likely to be?
pool.hint: Which type of text starts by telling you a tale is about to begin?
pool.explain: Once upon a time is a clue that a story is starting, with characters and something that happens.

pool.prompt: The cover says: by Lin Wu, pictures by Raj Dev. Who is the author?
pool.hint: The word by comes before the author's name. The pictures name is the illustrator.
pool.explain: Lin Wu wrote the words, so Lin Wu is the author. Raj Dev drew the pictures, so Raj Dev is the illustrator.

pool.prompt: A fact book about bugs has {n} labels on each page. How many labels are on 3 pages?
pool.hint: Labels name the parts in a picture. Add {n} three times.

pool.prompt: Where can you find the names of the author and the illustrator?
pool.hint: Look at the outside of the book, near the title.
pool.explain: Their names are on the front cover, near the title, and often on the first page inside too.

pool.prompt: A book has a shark on the cover. How can you find out if it is a story?
pool.hint: A shark could be in a story or in a fact book. What tells you which?
pool.explain: Look inside: characters and once upon a time mean a story; true facts and labels mean a fact book.

choices: No, some poems do not rhyme
pool.hint: Rhyme is a clue for a poem, but think about poems with short lines and no rhyming words.
pool.explain: Many poems rhyme, but some do not. Short lines and playing with sounds are clues as well.
